title: Order of Operations: BIDMAS with Brackets and Powers
seo_title: Year 7 BIDMAS Worksheets: Order of Operations with Brackets, Indices and Negative Numbers
standard_text: Use conventional notation for the priority of operations, including brackets, powers, roots and reciprocals.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 BIDMAS worksheets: multiply and divide before adding, brackets first, powers, negative numbers, fraction bars and writing calculations for word problems. 100 questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: BIDMAS: Brackets, Indices, Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction.
key_sub: D and M have equal priority, so do them left to right. The same is true for A and S.
body_html:
How it works

Use BIDMAS to decide what to do first:

  1. Brackets
  2. Indices (powers and roots)
  3. Division and Multiplication, left to right
  4. Addition and Subtraction, left to right

A fraction bar acts like a bracket around the top and around the bottom.

Example

Work out 5 + 3 × 4.

Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12.

Then 5 + 12 = 17.

Answer: 17

Example

Work out 2 × 3².

Index first: 3² = 9.

Then 2 × 9 = 18.

Answer: 18

Example

Work out 20 − 8 + 5.

+ and − have equal priority: go left to right.

20 − 8 = 12, then 12 + 5 = 17.

Answer: 17

Common mistakes

  • Working left to right: 5 + 3 × 4 is not 8 × 4 = 32.
  • Multiplying before the power: 2 × 3² is not 6² = 36.
  • Doing addition before subtraction: 20 − 8 + 5 is 17, not 7. D and M (and A and S) have the same priority.
  • Forgetting that (−3)² = 9 but −3² usually means −9.

faq.a: Brackets, Indices, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. It tells you the order to do a calculation.
No. Multiplication and division have the same priority, so you work from left to right: 48 ÷ 4 × 2 = 24.

faq.q: What is the difference between BIDMAS and BODMAS?
faq.a: Nothing. The O stands for Orders, another word for indices (powers).

faq.q: Why is 2 × 3² equal to 18 and not 36?
faq.a: The index is done before the multiplication: 3² = 9, then 2 × 9 = 18.

items.q: A cinema ticket costs £8 and popcorn costs £3. Four friends each buy a ticket and popcorn. Which calculation gives the total cost?
items.e: Each friend pays 8 + 3, and there are 4 friends, so the bracket is needed: (8 + 3) × 4 = £44.

items.q: Leo buys 3 pens at 45p each and a ruler at 60p. Which calculation gives the total in pence?
items.e: 3 pens cost 3 × 45, then add the ruler: 3 × 45 + 60 = 195p.

items.q: A class of 30 pupils is split into teams of 6, and 2 more teams join from another class. Which calculation gives the number of teams?
items.e: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 teams, then add 2 more: 30 ÷ 6 + 2 = 7.

items.q: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. Which calculation gives its perimeter?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width) = 2 × 11 = 22 cm.

items.q: Grace had £50. She spent £12 and then shared the rest equally with her sister. Which calculation gives how much each gets?
items.e: Take off the £12 first (bracket), then halve: (50 − 12) ÷ 2 = £19.

items.q: A taxi charges £3 plus £2 for every mile. Which calculation gives the cost of a 6-mile journey?
items.e: The £3 is paid once; the £2 is paid 6 times: 3 + 2 × 6 = £15.

items.q: The temperature was −4 °C. It rose by 3 °C each hour for 5 hours. Which calculation gives the new temperature?
items.e: The rise is 3 × 5 = 15 degrees, so −4 + 15 = 11 °C.

items.q: Ruby says 10 − 2 × 3 = 24. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Multiply first: 2 × 3 = 6, then 10 − 6 = 4. Ruby worked left to right.

items.q: Arjun says 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 36. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Square first: 32 = 9, then 2 × 9 = 18.
Division and multiplication have equal priority, so go left to right: 48 ÷ 4 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24.
Addition and subtraction have equal priority, so go left to right: 20 − 8 = 12, 12 + 5 = 17.
Bracket: 6. Then left to right: 36 ÷ 6 = 6, 6 × 3 = 18.
Inside the bracket, multiply first: 12 − 8 = 4. Then 3 × 4 = 12.
